memo.markdown:
## Verdict
The mandate verdict is Pursue [[mandate.verdict]]. The deal passes every hard filter and every soft test. Title is freehold single title, the area is in the mandate, and there is no master lease to a related party.

Recommendation: take Lantana Court to full diligence. Our walk-away price is AED 37.52m [[uw.walk_away_price_aed]], set by the levered IRR target. That is above the AED 36.00m [[deal.asking_price_aed]] ask, so there is headroom, but see the sensitivities below before using it.

## The deal
- Lantana Court, International City (OM says Phase 2, Warsan First), completed in 2016 [[deal.completion_year]], G+5 [[deal.floors]], 94 units [[om.unit_count]] (studios, 1BR and retail).
- Asking AED 36.00m [[deal.asking_price_aed]], or AED 719 per sq ft [[uw.price_per_sqft_nsa]] on NSA. On BUA it is AED 575 per sq ft [[uw.price_per_sqft_bua]].
- In-place contract rent is AED 3.82m [[rr.in_place_rent_aed]]. Occupancy by units is 95.74% [[rr.occupancy_by_units]], with 4 vacant units [[rr.vacant_units]]. All leases are direct, with no master tenant. Tenants pay chiller.

## Returns and key metrics
| Metric | Screen | Mandate |
|---|---|---|
| Year-1 NOI | AED 2.86m [[uw.noi_year1]] | none |
| Net yield on total cost | 7.49% [[uw.going_in_net_yield_on_cost]] | 6.00% [[mandate.min_going_in_net_yield_on_cost.threshold]] minimum |
| Year-1 DSCR | 1.90x [[uw.dscr_year1]] | 1.30x [[mandate.min_dscr_year1.threshold]] floor |
| Levered IRR, pre-tax | 9.68% [[uw.levered_irr_pre_tax]] | 8.00% [[mandate.target_levered_irr.threshold]] target |
| Equity multiple, pre-tax | 1.52x [[uw.levered_equity_multiple_pre_tax]] | 1.35x [[mandate.target_equity_multiple.threshold]] target |

The OM headlines 7.74% [[om.yield_stated]], net on total cost. On the buyer's basis, Year-1 NOI over price plus acquisition costs, it is 7.49% [[uw.om_yield.buyer_net_on_total_cost]]. The OM figure reproduces at 7.73% [[uw.om_yield.reproduced_on_om_basis]] on its own income, so the shortfall comes from our lower NOI, not from the OM's maths.

## What would make it fail
1. **Rent softens.** The IRR margin is thin. With market rent 5% [[uw.sens.rent_shift_step]] lower and the base exit yield, levered IRR is 7.42% [[uw.sens.r-5.e+0.levered_irr_pre_tax]], under the 8.00% [[mandate.target_levered_irr.threshold]] target. Add an exit yield 50 bps [[uw.sens.exit_shift_step_bps]] wider and it is 5.56% [[uw.sens.r-5.e+50.levered_irr_pre_tax]].
2. **Exit yield widens.** At base rent with the exit yield 50 bps [[uw.sens.exit_shift_step_bps]] wider, IRR is 7.86% [[uw.sens.r+0.e+50.levered_irr_pre_tax]], also under target. Base exit yield is 7.50% [[uw.exit_yield]]. Debt cover is not the issue: DSCR stays at 1.85x [[uw.sens.r-5.e+50.dscr_year1]] in the worst corner.
3. **Rollover.** The largest expiry window runs from 1 October 2026 [[uw.max_expiry_window_start]] to 31 December 2026 [[uw.max_expiry_window_end]]. It holds AED 1.17m [[uw.max_expiry_window_rent_aed]] of rent, or 30.67% [[uw.max_expiry_share_quarter]] of the total. That window falls before our 1 January 2027 [[uw.analysis_start]] start. It is inside the mandate limit of 40.00% [[mandate.max_lease_expiry_share_in_any_quarter.threshold]], but it is a large block to re-let or renew in a flat to falling market.
4. **Over-renting and cost.** Units let above market reference rent make up 5.42% [[uw.over_rent_share_of_income]] of income. That is small, and the reference market rent is above in-place rent. We underwrite opex at 25.00% [[uw.opex_ratio_year1]] of income against 23.33% [[opex.opex_ratio]] on the statement. If the operator's costs prove right, NOI is a little higher. We do not rely on that.

## Discrepancies that matter
The fact list contains no flagged discrepancies, so none are discussed here. The only material gap is the yield difference above: the OM's 7.74% [[om.yield_stated]] against our 7.49% [[uw.om_yield.buyer_net_on_total_cost]]. Occupancy is close: the OM says 96.00% [[om.occupancy_stated]] and the rent roll shows 95.74% [[rr.occupancy_by_units]]. The rent roll rent equals the OM's rent. The screen found no unverified OM fields.

## Before diligence, check
- Lease copies and renewal status for the units expiring in the largest three-month expiry window.
- Reconciliation of the 12-month operating statement to bank statements and invoices, covering service charge and sinking fund.
- The tenancy and legal status of the units under renewal and the one with notice served.
- Security deposits to be transferred to the buyer, and where they are held.
- Title deed, and confirmation of single freehold title.
- Evidence of current asking rents on vacant units and comparable market rents, to test the market rent reference.
- Confirmation of the NSA and BUA figures against the title documents.

## Assumptions
Debt is 45.00% [[assume.ltv]] LTV at 6.80% [[uw.interest_rate]] (EIBOR 4.30% [[assume.eibor]] plus margin 2.50% [[assume.margin]]), amortising over 20 years [[assume.amortisation_years]]. The hold is 5 years [[uw.hold_years]]. Exit yield is 7.50% [[uw.exit_yield]], which includes 25 bps [[assume.exit_yield_expansion_bps]] of expansion. We assume structural vacancy of 5.00% [[assume.structural_vacancy]] and collection loss of 1.00% [[assume.collection_loss]]. Renewal probability is 70.00% [[assume.renewal_probability]] and management fee is 5.00% [[assume.management_fee]] of income. Market rent moves -1.00% [[assume.rent_growth_year1]] in Year 1, 0.00% [[assume.rent_growth_year2]] in Year 2, then 2.00% [[assume.rent_growth_year3]], 3.00% [[assume.rent_growth_year4]] and 3.00% [[assume.rent_growth_year5]] in Years 3 to 5. No operating cost categories were filled from mandate defaults.
